Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI - Regulatory readiness & model risk (Northshore Health) — action & owners

Ack — taking technical lead. Initial clarifications / proposed approach:

1) NIST AI RMF mapping: we will provide a workbook that maps Redwood capabilities to the 4 functions (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage). For each control we will include: control owner, technical artifact (logs, dashboards), evidence sample (exportable JSON), and recommended customer config (e.g., cache TTL, tokenization settings).

2) EU AI Act positioning: Redwood is a runtime and platform. For classification: we provide guidance and an 'operator responsibility' section. For high-risk use cases (e.g., clinical decision support) we provide a conformity checklist, documentation package (technical file), model cards, provenance logs, and a suggested pathway for third-party conformity assessment where required. Stephanie — please vet the legal framing.

3) Continuous evaluation & regression testing: outline below (we will attach a full Evaluation_and_Regression_Plan.md):
   - Baseline suites: customer prompt-set + canonical benchmarks (privacy-preserving synthetic variants where needed)
   - Metrics: utility (task accuracy / F1), safety (hallucination rate measured by reference-checks), fairness signals (where labeled slices exist), latency/throughput SLO compliance, and drift (embedding-based distribution shift).
   - Automation: nightly data collection of labeled failures, weekly regression runs on canary model, and a gated rollout requiring <X% regression on critical test sets.
   - Rollback/mitigation: automated fallback to previous pinned model + routing to lower-capacity variant; incident ticketing and postmortem templates.

4) Evidence & attestations: we can provide SOC2 Type II report, penetration test summary, and exportable audit logs for a 90/365 retention window depending on plan (weʼll list available retention tiers).

Deliverables by 17 Nov: preliminary mapping workbook (Redwood_NIST_RM_Mapping.xlsx) and Evaluation_and_Regression_Plan.md. Full RFI answers and a PDF summary by 20 Nov.

Attaching draft artifacts for internal review.

— Aditya
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFI clarifications — EU AI Act & evaluation cadence

Thanks for the update, Aditya. A couple of clarifications from our side before you finalize the workbook:

1) EU AI Act: Northshore operates across the EU for some lines of business. For the purposes of the RFI, please explicitly state which Redwood features are intended to be used by the customer (operator) to meet documentation/conformity obligations. For example, do Redwood model cards + provenance logs meet the "documentation and record-keeping" article requirements, or would we need an additional compliance package?

2) Evaluation cadence: you mentioned nightly collection and weekly regression runs. For commissioned high-risk workflows we require a minimum quarterly third-party evaluation and monthly regression monitoring with automated alerts for any metric regressions >2% on our critical prompt set. Can Redwood support a monthly managed evaluation service and the ability to seed independent audits?

3) Data residency & logs: confirm that audit logs (inference inputs + model responses metadata) can be retained in EU regions and exported in CSV/JSON for up to 5 years under Private deployments.

If you can include short example artifacts in the workbook (sample model card, sample provenance log JSON, example regression report), that will speed our compliance committee review.

Regards,
Tom Reynolds
Head of AI Risk
Northshore Health

Subject: Re: RFI clarifications — EU AI Act & evaluation cadence — deliverables and next steps

Tom/Alice — thanks for the questions. Attached are the deliverables we discussed: a completed RFI summary PDF, the NIST mapping workbook with sample artifacts, and our evaluation & regression plan. Highlights and direct answers: 

- EU AI Act: Redwood provides a compliance support package for Private deployments in EU regions that includes: model cards (automatically generated per model version), provenance logs (structured JSON export of model lineage + inference metadata), a documentation template for the technical file, and optional assistance to integrate with third-party conformity assessors. These artifacts are intended to be used by the operator to fulfill documentation and record-keeping requirements; where a formal conformity assessment is required, Redwood will provide the technical file and evidence to the assessor but the operator is responsible for engagement with the notified body.

- Monthly managed evaluation: Redwood can offer a managed monthly regression monitoring service (subscription add-on). This includes monthly regression reports against your critical prompt set, automated alerts for >2% metric regression, and an annual/quarterly third-party audit option (we coordinate with accredited assessors). Pricing and SLAs for the managed service are in the attached PDF.

- Data residency & logs: for Private deployment we support EU-region retention of audit logs and export in CSV/JSON up to 5 years. Hosted plans can be configured with EU-region storage under our enterprise contract with limited retention tiers. Michael — please supply the retention tier matrix and any additional security controls they may request.

Next steps:
1) Weʼll upload the artifact bundle to the secure link: https://redwood.example.com/drive/RFI_NH_Nov2026 (DocuSign for any data processing addenda at https://docusign.com/envelope12345).
2) Proposal: if Northshore wants the managed monthly evaluation service, we can scope it in a statement of work.
3) Stephanie and I will prep draft contract language for EU AI Act operator responsibilities and upload redlines by 24 Nov.

Please confirm receipt and whether youʼd like a follow-up call next week to walk the compliance committee through the artifacts.

Thanks — Vanessa
